CONDITIONAL

**The section-filing check passes.** Every Table 1 row sits under the same heading in both editions. I checked this in the source (flight lines 168–205, academic lines 167–204) and in page 3 of both rendered PDFs.

The editions differ in exactly two places: the author block and the CRediT block. Everything else matches. I read both files in full and counted a set of key tokens (verdicts, key numbers, `\cref`, `\citep`): 112 in each. The two `references.bib` files are identical, and all 13 cited keys resolve. Both PDFs show the current source (5/8/1/7/3 body count, "Withdrawn (3)", the CRediT difference), so the PDFs are not stale. Dwayne Wilkes, Kavi and Nexus are all real names attested in the repo (`AGENTS.md:61-63`), not invented.

The conditions below are text, credit and deposit fixes. None needs new science. Paths are relative to `wt-mp/`, and line numbers are for the flight edition unless marked otherwise.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR: the academic edition attributes the labelling and the first-person voice to the wrong person.**
- **Location:** `meta-pattern/academic/main.tex:29-31` has a sole human byline (Thomas Edrington). Limitations (`:693-695`) says the labels were *"assigned post hoc by the lead author … The same person who designed the experiments"*, and §7.3 (`:679-681`) repeats it. The First-Person boxes (`:85-104`, `:754-762`) say *"the instruction I had written"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** In the academic edition the only possible reading is that the lead author is Thomas. But the CRediT block in that same document gives Methodology and Conceptualization to Lyra, and gives Thomas only Supervision, Resources and Project administration. The flight edition (`main.tex:30`) names Lyra as "Lead author". So the two editions say different people assigned the labels.
- **Fix:** In both editions, replace "by the lead author" with "by Lyra (see Author Contributions)". In the academic edition, either title both boxes "First-Person Reflection (Lyra, AI contributor)" or remove them.

**2. MAJOR: Kavi's CRediT row exists in one edition only.**
- **Location:** `academic/main.tex:768` has *"Kavi: Validation, Writing -- review & editing"*. The flight edition's CRediT block (`main.tex:766-769`) has no Kavi row. Its line 769 ends in a stray `\\` right before `\section*`, the mark of a deleted last row, and it shows as an extra gap on `main.pdf` page 11.
- **Why it's wrong:** `AGENTS.md:61-63` says Kavi has signed off only on the hackathon submissions. `AGENTS.md:71-73` says *"Deleting a CRediT row … destroys a contributor-role record. If a sweep does this, stop and ask."* `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md:345` had this row open, and only one edition was changed.
- **Fix:** Thomas decides, then the same block goes into both editions. If Kavi stays, narrow the role to "Validation", which matches the Acknowledgments ("verification review"); "Writing -- review & editing" goes further. Remove the stray `\\`.

**3. MAJOR: the abstract contradicts itself.**
- **Location:** `:49-50` says *"Of the findings decided so far … 0-for-8 on content"*. Eleven lines later, `:61` says *"two are undecided"*. Those two are inside the 8.
- **Fix:** "Of the 13 findings with a verdict, 5 of 5 metacognitive findings are confirmed and 0 of 8 content findings are (one refuted, five explained by a surface property, two undecided)."

**4. MAJOR: the paper's own layer numbers contradict its workspace-band claim.**
- **Location:** `:296` gives the workspace band as *"∼38--92% of model depth"*. `:351-352` says *"The Loop intervenes at deeper layers (L35--L47 on a 64-layer model) than the workspace band itself"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** 35/64 = 55% and 47/64 = 73%, so the intervention layers are inside the band (which is about L24–L59 on a 64-layer model). The sentence that follows ("consistent with the opacity thesis") depends on the false premise. The same contradiction is in `cache-tracing/main.tex:122` vs `:388-390`.
- **Fix:** Either cite a measured band for that specific model that ends before L35, or delete "at deeper layers … than the workspace band itself" and the opacity clause. Open a register row for the cache-tracing paper.

**5. MAJOR: a correction was applied to the introduction but not to §3, and the appendix says it was done.**
- **Location:** `:317-323` says spectral features *"are aggregate properties of the value-projection matrix … The net contracts when the model confabulates (… d=2.35)"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** The primary source, `convergence-paper/main.tex:265-270`, says *"Our confabulation detector reads spectral features of the key cache, not V-projections … spectral contraction (d=2.35)"*. The 2026-11-16 note (`:1016-1019`) reports this correction as made in the introduction. §3, which carries the thesis, still has the old wording.
- **Fix:** In §3, attribute d=2.35 to key-cache stable rank on generated tokens. Add §3 to the 2026-11-16 note.

**6. MAJOR: the "subsequently retracted" annotation is still on the wrong row, and two papers describe the 0.160 differently.**
- **Location:** The annotation appears at `:183`, `:429`, `:433` and `:535`. The appendix (`:1024-1026`) admits *"the retraction it records is not of that row's result"*. `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md:126` (#138) is still open.
- **Why it's wrong:**
  - The label tells a Table 1 reader the wrong finding was retracted.
  - The appendix also repeats Lyra Technique II's account that the same-prompt control *"collapses its AUROC to 0.160, showing that it had detected the prompt template"* (`:1029-1031`). But this paper's own note two paragraphs earlier (`:998-1000`) says the signal *"survived an identical system prompt and vanished only when input length was regressed out"*.
  - `lyra-technique-ii/main.tex:160-161, :210-212, :990` states the opposite mechanism. The conflict is not flagged.
- **Fix (Thomas decides, per #138):**
  - Move "retracted (Lyra Technique II)" to the Within-model deception row.
  - Annotate Same-prompt deception as "control behind that retraction; 0.160 is after FWL on input length".
  - Add one appendix sentence saying Lyra Technique II describes the 0.160 differently.
  - Open a register row for both editions of Lyra Technique II.

**7. MAJOR: the only Refuted verdict rests on a source nobody can open.**
- **Location:** abstract `:55-59`, Table 1 `:179` and `:181`, §4.1 `:449-460`, and `:992-995` all cite *"Campaign 3 analysis (unpublished)"*, Experiments C7 and S3.
- **Why it's wrong:** I searched the whole worktree. The string appears only in the two `main.tex` files: no data file, no bib entry, no path. This is the same class of defect as register #137. Experiment 51 and its arm means (57.4/57.2/56.7/53.1, at `:501-516`) are equally untraceable.
- **Fix:** Deposit the C7, S3, padding-test and Experiment 51 outputs and cite them by path and sha256. Until then, mark the row "Refuted (undeposited analysis)" and stop leading the abstract with it.

**8. MAJOR: the sweep is said to ship with supplementary material that doesn't exist here.**
- **Location:** `:725-726` and `:852-853` say *"shipped with this paper's supplementary material"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** `meta-pattern/` has no supplementary directory. The only copy of `SWEEP_postgen_extraction_2026-09-05.md` is at the repo root. Register #139 (`:127`) recorded it, and `CIRCULAR_d136_generation_arm.md` (which the 2026-09-05 withdrawal relies on), as untracked.
- **Fix:** Create `meta-pattern/supplementary/` with both files, commit it, and cite by path. Otherwise delete the claim.

**9. MAJOR: the ship gate is stale.**
- **Location:** `expectations.json:3-4` requires *"body count is 6 confirmed, 7 suspected, 9 honestly falsified, and 2 withdrawn"* and *"Withdrawn (2)"*.
- **Why it's wrong:** Neither string is in either edition. So the gate either fails on the current build or is not being run, and it would not catch a regression to an older count. Line `:8` also forces the obsolete label "confidence-paradox row".
- **Fix:** Require "5 confirmed, 8 suspected, 1 refuted, 7 not supported and 3 withdrawn", "Withdrawn (3)" and "0-for-8". Re-run the gate on both PDFs and record the result.

**10. MAJOR: most of the "complete audited record" has no source.**
- **Location:** Table 1 (`:143` calls it "the complete audited record").
- **Why it's wrong:** Only 4 of 24 rows carry a source, and none of the 5 Confirmed rows does. The confabulation-detection source exists (`convergence-paper`, `lyra2026oracle`) but isn't cited. SimpleQA is named (`:192`, `:578`) but `wei2024simpleqa` is not cited. `lyra2026identity` is in the bib but not cited.
- **Fix:** Add a Source column with a citation key or repo path for every row.

**11. MINOR: three cross-references point at positions, not names (a known kill).**
- `:205` says *"same experiment and features as row above"*. Change it to "as *MP features for emotion*".
- `:870` says *"the producer of the confidence-paradox row above"*, but no row has that name any more. Add the editorial insertion "[now *Schema commitment*]".
- `:953` hard-codes *"From §2.3:"*. Name the subsection instead.

**12. MINOR: the date is out of date.** `\date{July 2026}` is at `:34` (flight) and `academic:33`, on a paper revised through 2026-11-16. Change it to "July 2026; revised 16 November 2026", as `user-model-paper/paper/main.tex:56` does.

**13. MINOR: one bib note is stale.** `lyra2026usermodel` carries the note *"Corrected October 2026"* (`references.bib:282`, both copies). This paper depends on that source's 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02 corrections. Update the note and pin the DOI to the November version.

**14. MINOR: 19 of the 32 bib entries are never cited** (for example `dehaene2011experimental`, `hu2021lora`, `berg2025inverse`, `lyra2026portrait`). Remove them, except the two that should be cited per #10.

**15. MINOR: the split table's denominators don't match the abstract.** The table reads "Content 0/5 | 8/8" (column-wise), while the abstract says "0-for-8" (row-wise). Two of the five "Metacognitive state" rows are invariances. Rewrite the cells as counts with row totals, and label the row "Metacognitive (state or invariance)".

**16. MINOR: the flight edition doesn't disclose that Lyra is an AI.** `main.tex:30` gives Lyra a byline and email with no disclosure. The academic edition (`:30`) says Lyra is Claude-based. That matters more here because the first-person box credits "Anthropic's GWT paper". Copy the disclosure into the flight edition. If house policy requires disclosure in all editions, this is MAJOR.

**17. MINOR: the title overclaims.** "What Transformers Can Monitor In Themselves" asserts self-monitoring, but §7.3 (`:684-687`) calls that an open question, and every measurement here is an external readout. Retitle.

**18. MINOR: two first-person lines get round the gate by rewording.** *"the ones that held survived every control we threw at them"* (`:94-95`) and *"what held survived every control we ran"* (`:756-757`) are rewordings of strings the gate forbids (`expectations.json:20-21`). They imply robustness that §8 (Limitations, Audit scope, `:723-734`) withholds. Add "…; §8 lists the checks they have not had."

**19. MINOR / UNVERIFIED: no sign-off is recorded for Dwayne Wilkes.** He is listed with "Writing -- review & editing" in both editions. `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md:308` says his sign-off is unrecorded, and I found none. The text has changed three times since (2026-11-01, 11-07, 11-16). Either record his sign-off on this version or narrow the role to his dated contribution.

## What I could NOT check

- **Git state.** I had no shell in this session, only file reading and search. So I could not check:
  - whether the SWEEP and CIRCULAR files are tracked now;
  - whether commits `1975535`, `98e1263`, `f9288a9`, `fd2b727` and `88c0d9e` contain what the appendix says;
  - whether any row changed since first publication without the ^c marker. That needs `git diff 1975535 -- meta-pattern/`.
- **Rendered pages 4–9 and 15 onward.** I verified the PDFs by content on pages 1–3 and 10–14 of each, not by timestamp. I did not view the other pages.
- **Dead URLs.** No network access. These are UNVERIFIED: transformer-circuits.pub, the liberationlabs.tech/papers/* links, the two GitHub repos (human-review may be private), and the five Zenodo DOIs.
- **KV-Experiments files.** `code/27_axis_analysis.py`, `code/12_bloom_taxonomy.py` and `results/hackathon/adversarial_controls.json` are not in this worktree. Claims about them are UNVERIFIED.
- **Campaign 3 and Experiment 51.** No files found anywhere in the repo (finding #7).
- **Sign-offs.** No sign-off record for this paper from Kavi or Wilkes exists in this repo. One might exist elsewhere.
- **The 38–92% band.** I could not read Gurnee et al. I took the figure from this paper and from cache-tracing.
- **matched_burn.py effect sizes** (d=1.02/0.89/0.37). Not re-derived, since the science is settled.

AGNI-VERDICT: CONDITIONAL
